{"cluster_name": "grants_and_permissions_feature", "grouped_facts": [{"semantic_unique_id": "499d1533-1702-4058-a754-9f3f24132001", "fact": "dbt Core v1.2 introduced a `grants` config for resources", "quote": "In v1.2, we introduced a `grants` config", "technical_level": "configuration"}, {"semantic_unique_id": "dcf23df2-4536-4968-a8fc-af5c671bafa5", "fact": "`grants` is configured as a structured dictionary (e.g., {'select': ['role']}); dbt chooses the most efficient path to apply them", "quote": "You configure `grants` as a structured dictionary rather than writing all the SQL yourself\n* dbt will take *the most efficient path* to apply those grants", "technical_level": "implementation"}, {"semantic_unique_id": "b2699625-b9b0-4dfa-9275-7a33468c2849", "fact": "If `grants` is missing or set to {} dbt will not manage grants for that table", "quote": "if `grants` is missing or set to `{{}}`, dbt will understand that you don\u2019t want it managing grants for this table.", "technical_level": "configuration"}, {"semantic_unique_id": "86abe8c9-ac19-4580-8f59-ec0ce1e3c8d6", "fact": "When changing grants, dbt computes diffs and can issue REVOKE statements (visible in debug-level logs)", "quote": "you should see ... dbt has run a `revoke` statement.", "technical_level": "procedure"}, {"semantic_unique_id": "73994423-d6f8-4671-ba43-0b18d2f5c3ef", "fact": "dbt determines whether grants are 'carried over' for incremental models based on materialization and the target database", "quote": "It knows whether grants are \u201ccarried over\u201d when a model is re-run based on its materialization and your database.", "technical_level": "implementation"}, {"semantic_unique_id": "8a8b2872-bbce-4a3e-a5e1-4a0bc8c0a939", "fact": "`grants` config is exposed via dbt metadata/graph, allowing macros to iterate graph.nodes to infer schema-level grants", "quote": "Now that `grants` is a real config in dbt, available via dbt metadata, you can do all sorts of fun things with it. For instance, figure out which schemas have at least one object granting `select` to a role", "technical_level": "integration"}, {"semantic_unique_id": "42921dc7-7dc4-44cd-b968-1363f983fd51", "fact": "dbt does not treat schemas as first-class configurable objects; schema USAGE grants must still be applied via hooks", "quote": "there isn\u2019t really a way to configure *schemas as their own objects* within dbt.\nFor now, it\u2019s still necessary to grant `usage` on schemas", "technical_level": "constraint"}, {"semantic_unique_id": "08b864ac-d9ec-4ebe-b50d-ea460f26474a", "fact": "The 'manage grants' capability is global \u2014 users with the transformer role can change grants on any object as if they were the owner", "quote": "It is worth noting that this privilege *is* a global privilege \u2013 now anyone using the `transformer` role can change grants on any object as though they are the owner of the object.", "technical_level": "constraint"}, {"semantic_unique_id": "240d6771-7111-4976-90e3-04da4c1448d0", "fact": "Database-specific advanced permissions (Snowflake row access policies, masking) still require post-hooks to apply", "quote": "in Snowflake, you\u2019ll still want a `post-hook` to apply a [row access policy] or a column [masking policy] to your table", "technical_level": "procedure"}, {"semantic_unique_id": "9dbe9976-867b-45a4-b931-543737480e6c", "fact": "Use post-hooks to grant permissions to other transformers and BI users so model changes remain accessible to collaborators.", "quote": "Do you use post-hooks to grant permissions to other transformers and BI users? ... This will ensure that any changes made will be accessible to your collaborators", "technical_level": "procedure"}]}

{"cluster_name": "codegen_and_documentation_tooling", "grouped_facts": [{"semantic_unique_id": "f46efc19-a935-4373-a8d6-78e106f58328", "fact": "dbt Codegen macro generate_model_yaml requires model_names and supports upstream_descriptions (default=False).", "quote": "* `model_names` (required): The model(s) you wish to generate YAML for.\n* `upstream_descriptions` (optional, `default=False`): Whether you want to include descriptions for identical column names from upstream models.", "technical_level": "implementation"}, {"semantic_unique_id": "f17d6252-e060-4e23-a6e8-28556d234cbc", "fact": "generate_model_yaml accepts multiple model_names in one call to output a single combined .yml for several models.", "quote": "$ dbt run-operation generate_model_yaml --args '{{\"model_names\": [ \"activity_based_interest_activated\", \"activity_based_interest_deactivated\", \"activity_based_interest_updated\", ...] }}'", "technical_level": "procedure"}, {"semantic_unique_id": "34fa7bfb-1159-43a7-8ebf-415425c6f0f9", "fact": "Use dbt ls -m <path> --output name to programmatically list model names for piping into generate_model_yaml.", "quote": "$ dbt ls -m models/core/activity_based_interest --output name | xargs -I{{}} echo -n ' \"{{}}\",'", "technical_level": "procedure"}, {"semantic_unique_id": "299b09fc-8572-4de1-af31-42a7983d36bd", "fact": "Run dbt docs generate to validate YAML and surface syntax errors before running dbt docs serve.", "quote": "Run `dbt docs generate`. If there are syntax errors, this will be found out at this stage.", "technical_level": "troubleshooting"}, {"semantic_unique_id": "e9e5e8a0-f34c-4b05-9b97-a689ffcdcefd", "fact": "Create docs blocks with {{% docs <name> %}}...{{% enddocs %}} and reference them in schema YAML via {{ doc('<name>') }}.", "quote": "$ cat .../_activity_based_interest_docs.md  {{% docs activity_based_interest__id %}} ... {{% enddocs %}}\n$ cat .../_activity_based_interest_docs.yml  ... description: \"{{{{ doc('activity_based_interest__id') }}}\"", "technical_level": "integration"}, {"semantic_unique_id": "408129b9-c35f-4a5a-84d8-4498fc19d4ae", "fact": "When adding models or columns to an existing folder, prefer adding docs/doc-blocks manually rather than programmatic replacements.", "quote": "When adding additional models to a folder, or additional columns to an existing model, I would suggest adding new documentation and docs blocks manually rather than programmatically.", "technical_level": "procedure"}, {"semantic_unique_id": "ba81d07f-4b71-47f1-8f71-c4fa12c9ce68", "fact": "The solution was tested on Mac/VS Code; regex behavior may vary across environments (platform-specific regex caveat).", "quote": "Note that this solution has been tested on Mac/VS Code, and that regex behavior may vary between stacks.", "technical_level": "constraint"}]}
